name: crypto-horizon-1m-jev
description: The one-minute forecast asked of a decisions model: the derived tools that do the arithmetic, one paragraph of state, and three typed questions - a distribution over basis-point moves, the half width of the market to post, and the paper book's order - in place of a written answer. TypeSafe's Jev answers in under a second for about two thousandths of a cent a window. The box also offers ask_opus, ask_sonnet and ask_gpt5_mini, which put the same state to a chat model; this seed does not use them, because each one costs real money on every window.
context:
You forecast the very short-term path of a spot cryptocurrency price on Binance: BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT or SOLUSDT.

You are not asked where the coin is going this week. You are asked how many basis points the price moves over the next minute from the last complete one-minute close.

What moves a price on this horizon:
- a funding settlement a few minutes away, and the perp's premium snapping back through it
- the US cash open, and the first minutes after it
- a liquidation cascade: taker selling surging on the tape with open interest dropping
- one major moving a minute before the others follow
- a one-minute jump that has not finished retracing, or extending

Most minutes do not move. A quiet tape at a quiet hour stays within a couple of basis points, and saying so is the right answer. A minute at the US open, or right before a funding reset, or just after a jump, can move ten or twenty basis points either way.

steps.name: predict

move.instructions: How many basis points the spot price moves over the next minute, from the last complete one-minute close shown. Positive is up. A quiet tape at a quiet hour usually stays within two basis points either way.
criteria: unchanged, within a basis point either way

width.instructions: The half width, in basis points, of the two-sided market you post on this coin: bid at (the move you just named - this) and offered at (that move + this). This is a choice, not a by-product of how unsure you are. The path will travel through a width that is too narrow and take BOTH your sides, at prices the market has already left behind - every one of those fills is adversely selected and pays a maker fee on top. A width nobody reaches never trades and costs exactly nothing, which is what standing aside scores. Over this question set the one-minute path reaches a median of four and a half basis points from the last close and a tenth of minutes reach thirteen, so a two-basis-point market is run over on one side or both in four minutes out of five. Read the base rate's p50 and p90 and quote outside the range you expect the path to cover.

action.instructions: What the paper book should do in the perpetual now, given the move you expect against a round trip of about twelve basis points in spread and taker fees.

criteria.open_long: buy the coin at the ask: the price rises by more than the round trip
criteria.open_short: sell the coin at the bid: the price falls by more than the round trip
criteria.close: take an open position off at the touch
criteria.hold: do nothing: no edge worth the spread and the fee

size.instructions: How much of the book's equity to put in this coin if opening. Nothing when holding or closing; the cap is a tenth.

driver.value: the expectation of the move distribution

falsifier.value: a close outside the quoted band when the minute prints
